observation.what_happens: A red ball hanging from a black string swings side to side below a support. It is released from the right side and keeps swinging as a pendulum through the clip with no catch or stop visible.

calibration.note: black string = 0.6 m (narrator said thread length is sixty centimetres) spans 314 px in SAM's mask

given: scale: black string = 0.6 m (narrator said thread length is sixty centimetres) spans 314 px in SAM's mask, known to ±2%
thread length = 0.6 m (“धागे की लंबाई साठ सेंटीमीटर है।”)
reasoning: Theta oscillates about 0 with amplitude ~0.14 rad and period ~1.58 s on a constant-radius circle, matching a simple pendulum with L~0.62 m. Amplitude falls ~15% over 6.4 s, indicating weak damping in air. Candidates compete undamped linear textbook vs exact sine with linear viscous damping vs exact sine with quadratic aerodynamic drag.

law.title: Large-angle pendulum with viscous damping
law.summary: A real pendulum that slowly runs down because of friction proportional to speed.

fitted.title: Large-angle pendulum with viscous damping
fitted.summary: A real pendulum that slowly runs down because of friction proportional to speed.

candidates.ifItWins: The swing loses energy in proportion to speed from pivot friction and slow air viscosity, giving exponential amplitude decay.

law.title: Large-angle pendulum with quadratic air drag
law.summary: A pendulum slowed mainly by air resistance pushing harder when it moves faster.

fitted.title: Large-angle pendulum with quadratic air drag
fitted.summary: A pendulum slowed mainly by air resistance pushing harder when it moves faster.

candidates.ifItWins: Energy loss is dominated by turbulent air drag that grows as speed squared, not pivot viscosity.

law.title: Ideal small-angle pendulum
law.summary: A perfect frictionless playground swing that never loses energy.

fitted.title: Ideal small-angle pendulum
fitted.summary: A perfect frictionless playground swing that never loses energy.

candidates.ifItWins: The swing is a textbook undamped harmonic oscillator and the slow amplitude drop is just noise or sampling, needing no damping.

caveats: Thread length fixed from narration with about 2% scale uncertainty, which carries into gravity.
Linear and quadratic drag predict almost identically here, so air type is barely distinguished.
critique.finding: The ball swings side to side as a big-arc pendulum pulled by gravity with g = {g} on a thread of length L = {L}. It loses a tiny bit of motion each swing to air friction with damping {b}.

critique.why_it_won: It keeps the right gentle slowing as the swings get smaller, while quadratic air drag lets the motion stay too lively late on.

headline: Red ball swings as pendulum, air barely slows it
finding: The ball swings side to side as a big-arc pendulum pulled by gravity with g = 9.81 ± 0.2 m/s² on a thread of length L = 0.6 m. It loses a tiny bit of motion each swing to air friction with damping 0.0495 ± 0.00037 1/s.
